summary_plain: The Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment studied how gas flames behave, stabilize, and detach from burners in microgravity using the space station glovebox. Researchers burned different gas fuels to understand flame stability and soot formation without gravity's interference. This research helps improve fundamental combustion models and spacecraft fire safety.
summary_expert: The SLICE investigation utilized the Microgravity Science Glovebox and SPICE hardware on the International Space Station to study laminar diffusion flames. The experiment examined gas fuels including methane, ethylene, ethane, and nitrogen-diluted mixtures across testing experiments involving over 4,000 high-resolution images. Variables that changed between tests included the fuel composition, burner diameter, and coflow velocity. The documented findings describe objectives, apparatus design, and operational plans, noting that the operations started and completed in 2012.

key_findings.text: The SLICE investigation started and completed its operations on the ISS in 2012.
The apparatus captured more than 4,000 high-resolution images across 13 testing experiments.

earth_applications: cleaner, more efficient engines and industrial burners
